title: A studio backlot that became a skyline
lede: Century City was a movie backlot until 1961, when 20th Century Fox, short on cash, sold most of its land to Alcoa. Architects Welton Becket and Minoru Yamasaki turned the old sets into a planned city of towers, a grand hotel and a shopping center, and the Fox lot that remains still makes movies next door.
tl: Fox Film moves production to a large lot on Pico Boulevard west of Beverly Hills.
20th Century Fox sells most of its backlot to Alcoa, which plans a new city on it.
The open-air shopping center, today's Westfield Century City, opens.
The Century Plaza Hotel, designed by Minoru Yamasaki, opens.
Yamasaki's twin triangular Century Plaza Towers are completed.
Fox Plaza plays Nakatomi Plaza in Die Hard.

ch.h: From Western towns to office towers
p: For decades the hills between Beverly Hills and Cheviot Hills were a Fox backlot of Western towns, city streets and jungle sets. In 1961, with costs soaring, Fox sold most of the land to Alcoa, which hired Welton Becket to master-plan a city within the city: offices, apartments, a hotel and a shopping center, connected by wide boulevards including the Avenue of the Stars.

ch.h: Towers by the World Trade Center architect
p: Minoru Yamasaki, who would design New York's World Trade Center, designed the curved Century Plaza Hotel, which opened in 1966, and the twin triangular Century Plaza Towers, finished in 1975. The hotel hosted presidents and state dinners for decades and was restored and reopened in recent years.

The 35-story Fox Plaza, completed in 1987, became famous a year later as Nakatomi Plaza in Die Hard. The Fox studio lot right next door is still a working studio, so Century City remains one of the few places where the movie business and the office market share a fence line.

dyk: What was Century City before the towers?
The backlot of 20th Century Fox, sold to Alcoa in 1961.
Fox Plaza, completed in 1987 and featured in Die Hard in 1988.
Who designed the Century Plaza Towers?
Minoru Yamasaki, the architect of New York's World Trade Center.
lm: The curved hotel on Avenue of the Stars.
